messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: double exponential, wishart broken
parts:
The build problems are because these two distros
are failing unit tests (not failing to build).

I was wrong before -- Jenkins is catching this.

I'd still like the overall test to stop at the
test that fails. Or at least give me an option to
do that so I can see what's going to fail on Jenkins
before checking in. Is this possible?

- Bob

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] double exponential, wishart broken
parts:
Ok. I've done a few things with the make file:

1. The default make target, "make test-all", will fail on broken
tests. So either a compilation failure or a test failure will force
make to stop.

2. There is a new target: "test-unit". This will not fail on broken
tests. I tried to have all the tests included in one tests, which
would tell us how many passed and failed, but there's a duplicate
symbol in the unit tests somewhere.

3. Jenkins is calling "test-unit" so it will continue to call failed
builds ones where compilation fails and unstable builds ones where
compilation passes, but unit tests fail.

Bob, let me know if that's better behavior for the unit tests.


Daniel

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] double exponential, wishart broken
parts:
Daniel:

Thanks for patching double exp and Wishart.

Doing all the moves yesterday gave me a renewed
feeling for the scope of all these distribution
definitions.

I just looked up fabs() vs. abs().
We want to use fabs() in general because it's
defined for floating-point input whereas abs()
is only defined for int. So it must have been
casting our double args to ints and then applying
abs() and then casting back the returned int to
a double.

For tests, your second suggestion in (2) would
be perfect -- something that'll report at the
end which tests failed.

- Bob
